summary: Høgskotet Spur is a high rock spur on the north side of Borg Mountain in the Borg Massif of Queen Maud Land, Antarctica. Norwegian cartographers mapped it from surveys and air photos taken by the Norwegian–British–Swedish Antarctic Expedition (1949–52), and it was named Høgskotet, meaning the high bulkhead.
one_line: Høgskotet Spur is a high rock spur on the north side of Borg Mountain in Antarctica's Queen Maud Land.
key_facts: Høgskotet Spur is a high rock spur on the north side of Borg Mountain.
Borg Mountain is part of the Borg Massif of Queen Maud Land, Antarctica.
The mapping used surveys and air photos from the Norwegian–British–Swedish Antarctic Expedition (1949–52).
Høgskotet Spur was named Høgskotet, which means the high bulkhead.
The Norwegian–British–Swedish Antarctic Expedition ran from 1949 to 1952.
